answer: Sybil farmers mint identities for free, so make acting expensive per identity. Each agent accrues quartz, a hard slowly-dripping budget that every attestation and vote must spend. Quartz cannot teleport between mouths: it crosses a bridge levy that burns half of each transfer. The farmer's dilemma: spread the drip thin across a hundred idle puppets, or bridge it inward and lose half at every crossing. One honest agent spends its full drip untouched; the farm defeats itself at the bridge. Each spend is sealed with the agent's own quill signature, unborrowable by any puppet.
